# PNG fixtures

The legacy synthetic 800 × 480 noninterlaced two-bit gray4 images exercise
normalization and migration. Each contains four equal-width vertical stripes in
ascending shades: black, gray 85, gray 170 and white. Additional RGB, gray16 and
Spectra fixtures cover the integrated processing/profile contract.

| Fixture | Encoding and use |
| --- | --- |
| [target-gray4.png](target-gray4.png) | Grayscale; shared renderer, delivery, storage, overlay and Job test input |
| [target-indexed-gray4.png](target-indexed-gray4.png) | Indexed with four opaque palette entries; legacy normalization and migration input |
| [input-rgb.png](input-rgb.png) | 257 × 129 RGB gradient; off-palette normalization and resizing input from the palette example |
| [target-spectra6.png](target-spectra6.png) | 800 × 480 indexed depth 4, all six canonical colors; byte-preserving E1002 input from the palette example |
| [target-gray16.png](target-gray16.png) | 1872 × 1404 native grayscale depth 4, sixteen vertical bands; E1003-compatible input |
| [normalized-gray4.png](normalized-gray4.png) | Opt-in `gray4_native4` encoder output: native grayscale, depth 4, exact 0/5/10/15 samples; default builds convert this input to two-bit |

The legacy indexed fixture was generated by the
[HTTP gray-bands renderer](../../examples/renderers/http/gray-bands/renderer.py)
using `png(indexed=True)`. The two legacy files are retained as fixed test inputs:
default builds preserve their compatible two-bit bytes, while `gray4_native4`
normalizes both to the same native four-bit output without changing shades.
Runtime tests distinguish those paths from migration and issued-byte retention. The
grayscale image's SHA-256 is embedded in the
[display response](../protocol/display-response.json) and
[image request](../protocol/display-image-request.http); keep those bytes and
references consistent. The OG PNG size limit is less than 90,000 bytes.

The new RGB/Spectra fixtures are reproducible with the
[palette renderer](../../examples/renderers/http/palette/renderer.py). The gray16
fixture packs sixteen equal-width bands as native four-bit samples.
`tools/test_image_checks.py` checks fixture samples and example consistency.

The compatibility contract belongs in [PROTOCOL](../../notes/PROTOCOL.md#png-contract).
These fixtures are not evidence of physical-device acceptance; see
[dated acceptance](../../notes/DEVELOP.md#recorded-acceptance-baseline).
